gloss: to make progress; to advance smoothly

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {捗|はかど}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to make progress; to advance smoothly; to get a lot done
definitions.explanation: For work or tasks to progress well and efficiently. Often used to describe productive work sessions.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{捗|はかど}ったので、{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}れた。
examples.english: Work progressed well, so I was able to go home early.

examples.japanese: {静|しず}かな{環境|かんきょう}だと{勉強|べんきょう}が{捗|はかど}る。
examples.english: Studying goes smoothly in a quiet environment.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{全然|ぜんぜん}{捗|はかど}らなかった。
examples.english: I didn't make any progress at all today.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを{飲|の}むと{作業|さぎょう}が{捗|はかど}る。
examples.english: Work goes more smoothly when I drink coffee.

examples.japanese: {邪魔|じゃま}が{入|はい}らなかったので、{予定|よてい}よりも{捗|はかど}った。
examples.english: Since there were no interruptions, I made more progress than planned.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). No pair verb.

KANJI NOTE:
The kanji {捗|はかど} is not commonly used in everyday writing. This word is often written in hiragana as はかどる.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{仕事|しごと}が{捗|はかど}る (work makes progress)
・{勉強|べんきょう}が{捗|はかど}る (study goes well)
・{捗|はかど}らない (not making progress)

ANTONYM:
・{滞|とどこお}る - to stagnate, to be delayed

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in both casual and business contexts.

NOTE:
This is a popular word among Japanese internet users. The phrase 「{捗|はかど}る」 is often used when sharing productivity tips or discussing efficient workflows.
